On September 28, 2026, Gartner Japan announced the "Hype Cycle for Cloud and AI in Japan, 2026." It covers 31 advanced cloud and AI technologies, five of which are placed at the Peak of Inflated Expectations.
This article compares the text and Figure 1 of the 2026 press release with the chart from the 2025 press release, organizing a list by phase and the movement over the past year. The content is current as of October 5, 2026.
Gartner explains the Hype Cycle as a visual representation of how technologies and applications evolve over time, illustrating their maturity and adoption, as well as how they relate to solving real business problems and exploiting new opportunities.
Of the five items at the peak, only Frontier AI is explained in the text.
The five items at the peak are Frontier AI, FDE, Agentic AI, Physical AI, and Cloud Resilience.
Only Frontier AI is explained individually in the press release text; there are no explanations for FDE, Agentic AI, Physical AI, or Cloud Resilience.
Frontier AI is described as a core technology supporting the AI industrial revolution and is becoming a strategic foundation that influences corporate competitiveness and national technological sovereignty. It also notes that major vendors such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceX AI are accelerating the development race for Frontier AI equipped with more advanced reasoning capabilities and AI agent functions. Performance improvements are said to be driving transformation across a wide range of fields, including software development, R&D, business automation, and scientific computing.
Tadaaki Mataga, Distinguished VP Analyst, states the following:
"Frontier AI is highly likely to become the intelligence foundation for all future AI services and AI agents. For companies, the critical management issue is not 'whether to adopt it,' but 'which model to use and under what governance.'"
Risks are also mentioned. While companies that use it strategically can gain a new competitive advantage, the content notes that risks such as dependence on specific vendors, as well as the impact of geopolitical factors on supply restrictions, price fluctuations, and legal regulations, are also increasing. It states that in addition to performance, a comprehensive AI strategy that includes a multi-AI model strategy, sovereign AI, and data sovereignty will determine competitiveness.
Transcribing Figure 1: List of 31 items by phase
A list of the 31 items arranged by phase is not in the press release text. It is only in Figure 1. The following list is based on a visual reading of the positions and colors of the dots in Figure 1.
I will note one point: the dot for Hyper AI Supercomputers is just to the left of the boundary between the Innovation Trigger and the Peak of Inflated Expectations. Since it is close to the boundary, I am counting it as Innovation Trigger in this article.
The chart legend indicates the "years to mainstream adoption" using the shape and color of the dots. ○ (white) is less than 2 years, ● (light blue) is 2–5 years, ● (dark blue) is 5–10 years, ▲ is more than 10 years, and ⊗ is obsolete before reaching the Plateau of Productivity. There are no ⊗ items in the 2026 chart.
The bottom right of the chart says "As of August 2026."
The counts by phase are: 18 in Innovation Trigger, 5 in Peak of Inflated Expectations, 6 in Trough of Disillusionment, 2 in Slope of Enlightenment, and 0 in Plateau of Productivity.
The breakdown by years is: 4 items for less than 2 years (Frontier AI, Open-Weight Models, AI Model Routers, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)), 3 items for 5–10 years (Physical AI, QCaaS, Site Reliability Engineering), 2 items for more than 10 years (Space Computing, AI-Driven Cloud Computing), and the remaining 22 items are 2–5 years.
15 items disappeared from the 2025 version, 12 items added
The previous year's 2025 version had 34 items. The text listed them by dividing them into three perspectives: "AI and Industrial Revolution-related (17 items)," "Cloud-related (14 items)," and "Migration-related (3 items)." The 2026 text does not contain this perspective-based listing.

Of the 12 new items, two entered the Peak of Inflated Expectations—Frontier AI and FDE—while the remaining 10 are all in the Innovation Trigger.

'Multi-agent systems' (2025 version) is written as 'Multi-agent' in the 2026 version. In this article, I treat them as the same item and have not counted them as disappeared or newly added.
'AI agents,' which was at the Peak of Inflated Expectations, is not in the 2026 diagram; instead, 'AI agent platform' has been newly added to the Innovation Trigger. Whether it is the same item renamed or a different item is not stated in either press release. In this article, I count them as separate items.
The same applies to 'Cloud COE' (2025 version, Slope of Enlightenment) and 'AI platform COE' (2026 version, Innovation Trigger); their relationship is not mentioned in either press release. I count them as separate items.
Movement of the remaining 19 items: Agentic AI reaches the Peak of Inflated Expectations in one year
For the 19 items present in both diagrams, I have summarized the movement of their phases from the 2025 version to the 2026 version. Regarding the year markers, I also visually read and compared the colors of the dots in the 2025 diagram. For A2A protocols and M2C migration, the dots overlapped in the 2025 diagram and the colors could not be distinguished, so I have only written the markers for the 2026 version.
The three items that moved from the Innovation Trigger to the Peak of Inflated Expectations are Agentic AI, Physical AI, and Cloud Resilience. The three items that moved from the Peak of Inflated Expectations to the Trough of Disillusionment are New On-premises, V2C migration, and Re-virtualization. The two items that moved from the Trough of Disillusionment to the Slope of Enlightenment are IaC and Cloud-native.
The eight items that remained in the Innovation Trigger have all moved higher up the curve within the Innovation Trigger phase.

What is FDE: Explanations and predictions from the English press release the following day
The Japanese press release does not state what FDE stands for or how it is positioned in the Japanese context.
The day after the Japanese announcement, on September 29, 2026, Gartner (US) issued an English press release “Gartner Predicts 70% of Enterprises Will Abandon Agentic AI Built by Vendor Forward-Deployed Engineering by 2028”. It is crucial to be able to differentiate between the various process mining tools and technologies and to choose the right one for your organisation’s needs based on its goals and use cases to maximise intended value. There are two major categories of mining: “process” mining and “task” mining.
Processes are end-to-end groupings of logically related work, such as order-to-cash (OTC). Most of these end-to-end processes can be divided into subprocesses that group this logically related work into functions. In an OTC, subprocesses may include sales or accounts receivable. Each of these processes contains several tasks.
Tasks are the groupings of work within a process. For example, activities in the accounts receivable subprocess may include recording sales, generating invoices and tracking customer balances.
Process mining is a technique designed to discover, monitor and improve real processes (i.e., not assumed processes) by extracting readily available knowledge from the event logs of information systems. Process mining extracts process-related data from various digital sources such as enterprise resource planning (ERP), customer relationship management (CRM) and other operational databases that are readily available in today’s information systems.
With this information, process mining can be used to identify bottlenecks, inefficiencies and areas for improvement to enhance enterprise performance.
The tasks in Figure 1 (e.g., create sales order, schedule sales order) represent the “happy path” of the process, when there is no delay and no back-and-forth between tasks. However, this is generally not the case, and many business outcomes are impacted due to delays, assumptions and not adhering to the process.
Each task in the business process in Figure 1 has an associated event log. In the example, they are entries in an ERP system, a CRM system and a supply chain execution system. The task “notify customer” is manual with no event log attached to it; if this task shows a lot of variance in execution, it should be investigated.
After examining the outputs of the process mining algorithms, you can see what happened during the execution of the process to understand if there are areas for improvement. These could include discovering hidden aspects of the process, bottlenecks, conformance checking, or even finding opportunities to automate and enhance the process.
Planning: Identify areas within a process that have sufficient and high-quality datasets and are known to cause inefficiencies. Establish clear goals for the process mining initiative and determine what questions you hope to answer through the process analysis. The aim is to grow the process mining initiative gradually and connect the outcomes to the wider business initiatives.
Event logs: The starting point for process mining is an event log, which is a collection of digital traces that records the sequence of activities in a process.
Process discovery: This involves using process mining algorithms and techniques to analyse the process data and identify patterns, trends and areas for improvement.
Process optimisation: Use the insights gained from the process discovery to optimise the process, reduce inefficiencies and improve overall performance. This step can involve making changes to the process model, implementing new technology or changing business practices.
Implement: Once the process analysis is conducted, implement the changes into real processes and bring the insights to process owners and the relevant business stakeholders so they can act on the process findings.
Monitor and expand: Grow the process mining initiative over time and build out entire processes. Process mining requires continuous engagement that will involve members from across enterprise departments and hierarchies.
Task mining is a method of extracting valuable insights from low-level event data recorded in user interface logs or obtained through computer vision. The data captured includes individual steps performed by a user, such as keystrokes, mouse clicks and data entries, and is interpreted by utilising natural language processing (NLP) and optical character recognition (OCR) techniques.
Task mining complements process mining by providing a deeper understanding of the activities and actions taken within a process. The starting point for any task mining initiative is a user interface log. Each event found in a log refers to a step that is related to a particular task.
The events belonging to a task are ordered and can be seen as one sequence or routine of a task. For instance, consider the scenario where a user is responsible for pulling in invoices from an external system and navigates through multiple applications and screens to accomplish the task.
The steps that the user takes are to first download invoices from the directory of incoming invoices. The details of the invoices are then uploaded into an Excel sheet. Then the user logs into the accounting software – let’s say it’s an SAP system that requires the user to navigate through three different screens before the invoice data can be added into SAP.
All of these steps are completed by an employee at his or her desktop. Task mining will analyse the data collected during the execution of this task, collect variants and try to discover hidden aspects of the task and opportunities to enhance the task.
Process mining or task mining?
The main differences between process mining and task mining are that process mining targets end-to-end business processes (such as procure-to-pay and quote-to-cash) or parts of these processes, where different resources work together to deliver the process outcome – a product, service or information. In this case, the most granular unit is a task. Process mining is mainly interested in the order in which individual tasks are executed or evaluated, usually called the control flow.
Task mining targets a task consisting of different actions or steps. The granularity is a mouse click, keystroke, an entry of data or a desktop operation, such as copy/paste. Task mining is not only interested in the control flow (i.e., the sequence of the steps), but also in the data flow.
When looking at the data requirements of process mining compared to task mining, process mining begins with an event log, which includes events representing activities in a process and associated with a specific process instance. The event log requires an ID of the case, a description of the activity and a timestamp to determine the event sequence. Additional data such as amount, location and client can be used for more comprehensive analysis.
From a data perspective, task mining requires step information and timestamps for sequencing, but it lacks a unique identifier such as process mining. To determine the control flow, task mining first segments the captured data to identify repetitive routines and then analyses the data introduced and its composition. It requires more comprehensive data than process mining, especially for process discovery or robotic process mining use cases.
Gartner regards process mining as a special case of data mining. Unlike data mining, process mining focuses on the process perspective. It includes the temporal aspect and looks at a single process execution as a sequence of activities that have been performed.
Process mining bridges the gap between data mining and the modelling, control and improvement of business processes. Going forward, Gartner expects process mining and analysis will evolve to process intelligence that combines development and runtime software tools to analyse, model, and monitor business processes.
Task mining combines process mining techniques and specific algorithms for case segmentation and data pattern recognition. NLP may be used to identify and extract key data, and computer vision and screen capturing may be utilised in robotic process automation (RPA) use cases to create or improve user interface logs.

REDWOOD CITY, Calif., Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Simpplr, the AI-powered intranet for unifying the digital workplace, today announced that Gartner has positioned Simpplr as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Intranet Packaged Solutions. The recognition comes as the role of the intranet is rapidly changing. Employees still need clear, trusted communications. Increasingly, they also need one place to find answers, access services, and take action across a fragmented digital workplace.
"Four years ago, this category was largely about helping employees find information and stay connected. That still matters. But the problem has gotten bigger," said Dhiraj Sharma, CEO of Simpplr. That's the problem we're building Simpplr to solve."

Simpplr believes its continued recognition reflects both the evolution of its platform and its focus on translating innovation into practical value for customers. The company identifies emerging buyer and technology trends and turns them into delivered innovation, most recently advancing AI for employee communications and governance. Simpplr pairs that with a structured customer engagement model built to accelerate time-to-value, including standardized delivery, dedicated Customer Success Managers, and embedded adoption.
"For us, Simpplr's continued recognition as a Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant is a testament to their commitment to innovation and customer success," says Wyatt Semanek, Director of Corporate Communications at Sunrun. "The platform has been instrumental in enhancing employee engagement and productivity across our diverse workforce."
The next generation of the intranet has to do more than publish information. It has to help employees use it.
In the accompanying 2026 Gartner Critical Capabilities for Intranet Packaged Solutions, Gartner recognizes Simpplr and ranks them across Use Cases including Knowledge Services, Employee & Workplace Services, and Work Management.
Simpplr brings trusted information and everyday action closer together. Enterprise search and Smart Answers help employees find what they need. EX Agent provides conversational self-service and guided next steps. App Tiles consolidate operational systems into role-specific mini-apps that centralize actionable tasks such as scheduling, training, and service requests.
The result is a simpler path from question to outcome — without requiring employees to know where information lives, which system owns a process or what application comes next.
As work becomes more complex, the employee experience shouldn't.
Simpplr embeds AI across the employee experience rather than treating it as another tool employees have to seek out. AI-powered search, assistants, agents, personalization and automation help employees find answers, access services and take action, while capabilities such as AI Control Center and Agent Studio give IT teams governance over knowledge, permissions, and actions.
That experience extends across office, distributed, and frontline workforces. Simpplr's mobile-first capabilities, shared-device support, one-time passwords and granular access controls — helping employees access trusted knowledge, communications, and services wherever work happens.
The goal is simple: use AI to make work easier for employees, while keeping the complexity of enterprise systems behind the scenes.

Gartner "Hype Cycle for Cloud and AI in Japan, 2026": Transcribed 31 Items from the Chart
On September 28, 2026, Gartner Japan announced the "Hype Cycle for Cloud and AI in Japan, 2026." It covers 31 advanced cloud and AI technologies, five of which are placed at the Peak of Inflated Expectations.
This article compares the text and Figure 1 of the 2026 press release with the chart from the 2025 press release, organizing a list by phase and the movement over the past year. The content is current as of October 5, 2026.
Gartner explains the Hype Cycle as a visual representation of how technologies and applications evolve over time, illustrating their maturity and adoption, as well as how they relate to solving real business problems and exploiting new opportunities.
Of the five items at the peak, only Frontier AI is explained in the text.
The five items at the peak are Frontier AI, FDE, Agentic AI, Physical AI, and Cloud Resilience.
Only Frontier AI is explained individually in the press release text; there are no explanations for FDE, Agentic AI, Physical AI, or Cloud Resilience.
Frontier AI is described as a core technology supporting the AI industrial revolution and is becoming a strategic foundation that influences corporate competitiveness and national technological sovereignty. It also notes that major vendors such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceX AI are accelerating the development race for Frontier AI equipped with more advanced reasoning capabilities and AI agent functions. Performance improvements are said to be driving transformation across a wide range of fields, including software development, R&D, business automation, and scientific computing.
Tadaaki Mataga, Distinguished VP Analyst, states the following:
"Frontier AI is highly likely to become the intelligence foundation for all future AI services and AI agents. For companies, the critical management issue is not 'whether to adopt it,' but 'which model to use and under what governance.'"
Risks are also mentioned. While companies that use it strategically can gain a new competitive advantage, the content notes that risks such as dependence on specific vendors, as well as the impact of geopolitical factors on supply restrictions, price fluctuations, and legal regulations, are also increasing. It states that in addition to performance, a comprehensive AI strategy that includes a multi-AI model strategy, sovereign AI, and data sovereignty will determine competitiveness.
Transcribing Figure 1: List of 31 items by phase
A list of the 31 items arranged by phase is not in the press release text. It is only in Figure 1. The following list is based on a visual reading of the positions and colors of the dots in Figure 1.
I will note one point: the dot for Hyper AI Supercomputers is just to the left of the boundary between the Innovation Trigger and the Peak of Inflated Expectations. Since it is close to the boundary, I am counting it as Innovation Trigger in this article.
The chart legend indicates the "years to mainstream adoption" using the shape and color of the dots. ○ (white) is less than 2 years, ● (light blue) is 2–5 years, ● (dark blue) is 5–10 years, ▲ is more than 10 years, and ⊗ is obsolete before reaching the Plateau of Productivity. There are no ⊗ items in the 2026 chart.
The bottom right of the chart says "As of August 2026."
The counts by phase are: 18 in Innovation Trigger, 5 in Peak of Inflated Expectations, 6 in Trough of Disillusionment, 2 in Slope of Enlightenment, and 0 in Plateau of Productivity.
The breakdown by years is: 4 items for less than 2 years (Frontier AI, Open-Weight Models, AI Model Routers, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)), 3 items for 5–10 years (Physical AI, QCaaS, Site Reliability Engineering), 2 items for more than 10 years (Space Computing, AI-Driven Cloud Computing), and the remaining 22 items are 2–5 years.
15 items disappeared from the 2025 version, 12 items added
The previous year's 2025 version had 34 items. The text listed them by dividing them into three perspectives: "AI and Industrial Revolution-related (17 items)," "Cloud-related (14 items)," and "Migration-related (3 items)." The 2026 text does not contain this perspective-based listing.
The number of items by phase in the diagram for the 2025 version was: 17 in the Innovation Trigger, 7 at the Peak of Inflated Expectations, 7 in the Trough of Disillusionment, 3 in the Slope of Enlightenment, and 0 on the Plateau of Productivity.
Comparing the two diagrams, there are 15 items that were in the 2025 version but are not in the 2026 version, and 12 items that are new in the 2026 version. The reasons for their disappearance are not mentioned in either press release.
Of the 12 new items, two entered the Peak of Inflated Expectations—Frontier AI and FDE—while the remaining 10 are all in the Innovation Trigger.
I will provide three supplementary points regarding how the items are counted.
'Multi-agent systems' (2025 version) is written as 'Multi-agent' in the 2026 version. In this article, I treat them as the same item and have not counted them as disappeared or newly added.
'AI agents,' which was at the Peak of Inflated Expectations, is not in the 2026 diagram; instead, 'AI agent platform' has been newly added to the Innovation Trigger. Whether it is the same item renamed or a different item is not stated in either press release. In this article, I count them as separate items.
The same applies to 'Cloud COE' (2025 version, Slope of Enlightenment) and 'AI platform COE' (2026 version, Innovation Trigger); their relationship is not mentioned in either press release. I count them as separate items.
Movement of the remaining 19 items: Agentic AI reaches the Peak of Inflated Expectations in one year
For the 19 items present in both diagrams, I have summarized the movement of their phases from the 2025 version to the 2026 version. Regarding the year markers, I also visually read and compared the colors of the dots in the 2025 diagram. For A2A protocols and M2C migration, the dots overlapped in the 2025 diagram and the colors could not be distinguished, so I have only written the markers for the 2026 version.
The three items that moved from the Innovation Trigger to the Peak of Inflated Expectations are Agentic AI, Physical AI, and Cloud Resilience. The three items that moved from the Peak of Inflated Expectations to the Trough of Disillusionment are New On-premises, V2C migration, and Re-virtualization. The two items that moved from the Trough of Disillusionment to the Slope of Enlightenment are IaC and Cloud-native.
The eight items that remained in the Innovation Trigger have all moved higher up the curve within the Innovation Trigger phase.
The 2025 press release stated: 'Many innovations in the AI field tend to be prone to hype. Among them, "Agentic AI," which has been attracting attention in recent years, is a typical example.'
At the time, Mr. Mataga stated, 'Companies need to be mindful of AI agent washing, correctly recognize the gap between their future ideal image and the "reality" that can be achieved at present, and calmly determine the introduction strategy and deployment timing that suits their company without falling into excessive expectations or underestimation.'
One year later, Agentic AI moved from the Innovation Trigger to the Peak of Inflated Expectations.
The same 2025 version also contained the statement: 'Gartner believes that AI will reach maturity at a relatively early stage. On the other hand, although a considerable amount of time has passed since the emergence of cloud-related technologies, their utilization in companies remains limited, and maturity is taking longer than expected.'
Sovereign cloud moves to the Trough of Disillusionment without passing through the Peak of Inflated Expectations
Sovereign cloud was just before the Peak of Inflated Expectations in the Innovation Trigger in the 2025 version, and is in the middle of the Trough of Disillusionment in the 2026 version. On the diagram, it appears to have entered the Trough of Disillusionment without passing through the Peak of Inflated Expectations. The reason is not written in the press release.
Comparing the colors of the dots, five items have changed their year markers. Agentic AI, MCP, World Model, and New On-premises have moved from 5–10 years to 2–5 years, while QCaaS has moved from more than 10 years to 5–10 years. All are trending toward shorter timeframes. Physical AI and Site Reliability Engineering remain at 5–10 years, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) remains at less than 2 years.
What is FDE: Explanations and predictions from the English press release the following day
The Japanese press release does not state what FDE stands for or how it is positioned in the Japanese context.
The day after the Japanese announcement, on September 29, 2026, Gartner (US) issued an English press release “Gartner Predicts 70% of Enterprises Will Abandon Agentic AI Built by Vendor Forward-Deployed Engineering by 2028”. Although no direct link to the Japanese press release is mentioned, the explanation of FDE is provided there.
In the English press release, FDE is used as an abbreviation for forward-deployed engineering, described as a model (vendor FDE) where vendor engineers work directly with customers to build and deploy solutions.
Prediction 1: By 2028, 70% of enterprises will abandon agentic AI built by vendor FDE. The reasons cited are high costs and the inability to evolve the systems in-house.
Prediction 2: By 2028, less than 20% of FDE engagements will convert recurring customer needs into features of the vendor's core product. It notes that the risk of “FDE washing,” where consulting services are sold under the guise of FDE, is increasing.
The speaker is Senior Director Analyst Mukul Saha. He states that many providers are using “forward-deployed” as a label for implementation, professional services, solution engineering, and AI consulting.
Cloud is becoming AI-driven; cloud strategy is talent strategy
The remaining points in the Japanese press release concern the positioning of the cloud and talent.
Regarding the AI field as a whole, Gartner observes that because vendor investment is extremely active and interest and practice among user companies are rising rapidly, many technologies will mature in a relatively short period. On the other hand, it predicts that the market centered on agentic AI will continue to evolve rapidly.
The press release states that about 20 years have passed since the emergence of hyperscalers, and the cloud has become an essential foundation for enterprises. It positions AI and cloud as mutually evolving, with the cloud shifting from a foundation for using AI to an “AI-driven cloud” designed and operated with AI at its core. This paradigm shift is said to be changing not only the role of the cloud but also corporate IT strategy, business strategy, and the competitive environment itself.
A statement from Mr. Mataga:
“The cloud is transforming from a mere extension of traditional IT infrastructure into a strategic platform for building, executing, connecting, and operating AI agents. Enterprises need to position the cloud as a management foundation that supports continuous innovation. Moving forward, it will be the evolution of the cloud foundation supporting AI, not just AI itself, that determines corporate competitiveness.”
It is written that the transition to an AI-driven cloud cannot be achieved simply by introducing technology. The press release states that it is essential for everyone from management to the front lines to continuously improve their knowledge and capabilities regarding AI, cloud, and platform engineering.
Mr. Mataga states, “Competitiveness in the AI era is determined not by the technology itself, but by the talent and organization that use it to create value. Cloud strategy is also talent strategy.”

Gartner Inc. stock (ISIN US3666511072) is trading at 186.42 USD as of September 7, 2026, down 4.62 percent on the day despite the company reporting a clear earnings beat in its latest quarter and guiding to double-digit earnings per share for 2026.IT BOLTWISE
Strong quarterly figures and 2026 EPS guidance
According to IT BOLTWISE, Gartner has set an earnings per share guidance of 14.00 USD for fiscal year 2026, signaling a double-digit EPS level that underscores management’s confidence in the medium-term profit trajectory for the research and advisory group.IT BOLTWISE In the most recently reported quarter, identified as Q2 2026 in market commentary, Gartner delivered EPS of 4.37 USD versus a consensus expectation of 3.76 USD, beating estimates by 0.61 USD per share.IT BOLTWISE The same source reports quarterly revenue of 1.68 billion USD compared with 1.65 billion USD expected, a modest top-line beat of 30.0 million USD that still confirms the company’s ability to grow beyond market assumptions.IT BOLTWISE
IT BOLTWISE also highlights that Gartner’s net margin stands at around 11.99 percent in the latest reported period, reflecting a solid level of profitability for a subscription-driven research and consulting model.IT BOLTWISE For investors, the key point is that earnings and revenue both came in ahead of consensus in Q2 2026 while the 2026 EPS guidance remains in clearly double-digit territory, yet the share price does not fully mirror that operational strength in early September 2026.IT BOLTWISE
Analyst targets and technical signals remain cautious
MarketBeat data show that Gartner currently carries a consensus rating of Hold among covering analysts, with an average target price of 187.30 USD, only slightly above the 186.42 USD trading level cited for September 7, 2026.MarketBeat This narrow gap suggests limited expected upside from current prices based on the existing analyst models, even after the recent earnings beats. One compilation notes that one analyst has a Strong Buy rating, two have Buy ratings, six rate Gartner as Hold and two assign Sell ratings, underlining the mixed view on the stock.MarketBeat
In parallel, IT BOLTWISE reports that technical indicators for Gartner’s shares currently point to selling pressure: on a daily view, the technical analysis framework sends a Sell signal, and on a one-week basis, the signals even strengthen to a Strong Sell assessment.IT BOLTWISE The same analysis notes that over the past twelve months the stock has declined by 48.46 percent, a sharp drawdown that frames the recent daily moves within a broader negative trend.IT BOLTWISE For investors this creates a tension between strong recent fundamentals and a price chart that still reflects significant skepticism.
Current price, valuation and market comparison
On September 7, 2026, Pluang’s comparison overview shows Gartner trading at 186.42 USD, down 4.62 percent on the day, with recent technical support identified around 185 USD.Pluang The same source cites a market capitalization of 11.77 billion USD for Gartner, giving a sense of the company’s mid-cap scale in the US equity market as of early September 2026.Pluang That overview also mentions that Gartner’s price-earnings ratio stands around 16.76, which is described as below industry averages, suggesting that the stock’s valuation is not stretched despite the recent operational strength.Pluang
Pluang’s data further point to a gross margin of 69.63 percent and a net income margin of 12 percent for Gartner, in line with the roughly 11.99 percent net margin highlighted by IT BOLTWISE for the latest reported period.PluangIT BOLTWISE This margin profile confirms that Gartner’s research and subscription model remains highly profitable. However, Pluang also notes that negative net cash flow trends, such as a minus 211 million USD figure in 2025, and a very high price-to-book ratio around 160.06 raise balance sheet and valuation concerns.Pluang Combined with an analyst consensus that is only 27.78 percent Buy and a price target of 178.33 USD below the current price level, these data underscore that the market sees limited near-term upside despite operational momentum.Pluang
Research and advisory business drives results
Gartner, headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, is a global provider of independent research, advisory services and conferences focused on information technology and digital transformation.Pluang Its core business model centers on subscription-based research offerings and strategic consulting engagements aimed at chief information officers and other senior executives who shape corporate IT budgets.Pluang IT BOLTWISE emphasizes that recurring research subscriptions and long-term advisory contracts help stabilize revenue and margin, supporting the double-digit net margin reported in the latest period.IT BOLTWISE
For investors, this setup means that Gartner’s earnings and cash flows depend less on one-off projects and more on renewing subscriptions and maintaining high customer retention in its research segments. The recent beat on Q2 2026 revenue to 1.68 billion USD versus 1.65 billion USD expected shows that this engine still delivers growth above analyst assumptions.IT BOLTWISE At the same time, risks highlighted in market commentary include potential weakness in consulting segments and ongoing shareholder investigations mentioned in Pluang’s summary, both of which could weigh on sentiment even as the core research franchise remains strong.Pluang
Representative Gartner conferences as a product anchor
One representative product area for Gartner is its global portfolio of IT conferences and events, where the company brings together CIOs, technology vendors and enterprise leaders around topics such as cloud, cybersecurity and data strategy.Pluang These conferences complement the research and advisory products by driving customer engagement and generating incremental consulting leads tied to digital transformation projects. While specific event revenue figures are not detailed in the recent sources, the sustained double-digit net margin around 12 percent in Q2 2026 indicates that the mix of subscriptions, consulting and conferences collectively supports Gartner’s profitability.IT BOLTWISEPluang
Gartner Inc. stock below analyst target but supported by fundamentals
As of September 7, 2026, Gartner’s reference price on its primary listing in the United States stands at 186.42 USD, with technical support discussed near 185 USD and an average analyst target price of 187.30 USD only marginally above that level.PluangMarketBeat Pluang’s overview assigns Gartner a market capitalization of 11.77 billion USD, reflecting its position as a sizeable mid-cap within the US technology and business services landscape.Pluang Against this valuation backdrop, the Q2 2026 EPS beat of 0.61 USD over consensus and the modest revenue outperformance of 30.0 million USD suggest that the company’s operations are ahead of prior expectations, even if the stock price still lags its historical levels.IT BOLTWISE

Gartner (IT) faces low Street expectations for Q3 contract value growth that a total beat is possible even as weakness outside the federal business persists, UBS said in a Monday note.
UBS said a beat could help the stock sustain its recent momentum, even though some investors view the recent strength as a squeeze or bounce, adding that continued ex-federal softness will likely perpetuate the longstanding bear narrative.
The firm said it expects total contract value growth of 2.5% in Q3, versus the Street's 2.3%. It cut its ex-federal net contract value increase estimate to $45 million from $60 million prior, citing a difficult renewal and selling environment, while a moderate recovery in the federal business offsets some of the weakness.
UBS expects Gartner to raise its 2026 earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization as well as earnings per share guidance, primarily due to margin contingency, and sees a modest increase in the revenue guide. It also expects a noticeably lower pace of share buybacks in Q3.
UBS maintained it neutral rating and raised its price target to $208 per share from $196.

The field of process mining has grown rapidly in recent years, and with the increasing adoption of digital technologies and data-driven business processes, it has become increasingly important to understand the tools and techniques available.
It is crucial to be able to differentiate between the various process mining tools and technologies and to choose the right one for your organisation’s needs based on its goals and use cases to maximise intended value. There are two major categories of mining: “process” mining and “task” mining.
Processes are end-to-end groupings of logically related work, such as order-to-cash (OTC). Most of these end-to-end processes can be divided into subprocesses that group this logically related work into functions. In an OTC, subprocesses may include sales or accounts receivable. Each of these processes contains several tasks.
Tasks are the groupings of work within a process. For example, activities in the accounts receivable subprocess may include recording sales, generating invoices and tracking customer balances.
Process mining is a technique designed to discover, monitor and improve real processes (i.e., not assumed processes) by extracting readily available knowledge from the event logs of information systems. Process mining extracts process-related data from various digital sources such as enterprise resource planning (ERP), customer relationship management (CRM) and other operational databases that are readily available in today’s information systems.
With this information, process mining can be used to identify bottlenecks, inefficiencies and areas for improvement to enhance enterprise performance.
The tasks in Figure 1 (e.g., create sales order, schedule sales order) represent the “happy path” of the process, when there is no delay and no back-and-forth between tasks. However, this is generally not the case, and many business outcomes are impacted due to delays, assumptions and not adhering to the process.
Each task in the business process in Figure 1 has an associated event log. In the example, they are entries in an ERP system, a CRM system and a supply chain execution system. The task “notify customer” is manual with no event log attached to it; if this task shows a lot of variance in execution, it should be investigated.
After examining the outputs of the process mining algorithms, you can see what happened during the execution of the process to understand if there are areas for improvement. These could include discovering hidden aspects of the process, bottlenecks, conformance checking, or even finding opportunities to automate and enhance the process.
Planning: Identify areas within a process that have sufficient and high-quality datasets and are known to cause inefficiencies. Establish clear goals for the process mining initiative and determine what questions you hope to answer through the process analysis. The aim is to grow the process mining initiative gradually and connect the outcomes to the wider business initiatives.
Event logs: The starting point for process mining is an event log, which is a collection of digital traces that records the sequence of activities in a process.
Process discovery: This involves using process mining algorithms and techniques to analyse the process data and identify patterns, trends and areas for improvement.
Process optimisation: Use the insights gained from the process discovery to optimise the process, reduce inefficiencies and improve overall performance. This step can involve making changes to the process model, implementing new technology or changing business practices.
Implement: Once the process analysis is conducted, implement the changes into real processes and bring the insights to process owners and the relevant business stakeholders so they can act on the process findings.
Monitor and expand: Grow the process mining initiative over time and build out entire processes. Process mining requires continuous engagement that will involve members from across enterprise departments and hierarchies.
Task mining is a method of extracting valuable insights from low-level event data recorded in user interface logs or obtained through computer vision. The data captured includes individual steps performed by a user, such as keystrokes, mouse clicks and data entries, and is interpreted by utilising natural language processing (NLP) and optical character recognition (OCR) techniques.
Task mining complements process mining by providing a deeper understanding of the activities and actions taken within a process. The starting point for any task mining initiative is a user interface log. Each event found in a log refers to a step that is related to a particular task.
The events belonging to a task are ordered and can be seen as one sequence or routine of a task. For instance, consider the scenario where a user is responsible for pulling in invoices from an external system and navigates through multiple applications and screens to accomplish the task.
The steps that the user takes are to first download invoices from the directory of incoming invoices. The details of the invoices are then uploaded into an Excel sheet. Then the user logs into the accounting software – let’s say it’s an SAP system that requires the user to navigate through three different screens before the invoice data can be added into SAP.
All of these steps are completed by an employee at his or her desktop. Task mining will analyse the data collected during the execution of this task, collect variants and try to discover hidden aspects of the task and opportunities to enhance the task.
Process mining or task mining?
The main differences between process mining and task mining are that process mining targets end-to-end business processes (such as procure-to-pay and quote-to-cash) or parts of these processes, where different resources work together to deliver the process outcome – a product, service or information. In this case, the most granular unit is a task. Process mining is mainly interested in the order in which individual tasks are executed or evaluated, usually called the control flow.
Task mining targets a task consisting of different actions or steps. The granularity is a mouse click, keystroke, an entry of data or a desktop operation, such as copy/paste. Task mining is not only interested in the control flow (i.e., the sequence of the steps), but also in the data flow.
When looking at the data requirements of process mining compared to task mining, process mining begins with an event log, which includes events representing activities in a process and associated with a specific process instance. The event log requires an ID of the case, a description of the activity and a timestamp to determine the event sequence. Additional data such as amount, location and client can be used for more comprehensive analysis.
From a data perspective, task mining requires step information and timestamps for sequencing, but it lacks a unique identifier such as process mining. To determine the control flow, task mining first segments the captured data to identify repetitive routines and then analyses the data introduced and its composition. It requires more comprehensive data than process mining, especially for process discovery or robotic process mining use cases.
Gartner regards process mining as a special case of data mining. Unlike data mining, process mining focuses on the process perspective. It includes the temporal aspect and looks at a single process execution as a sequence of activities that have been performed.
Process mining bridges the gap between data mining and the modelling, control and improvement of business processes. Going forward, Gartner expects process mining and analysis will evolve to process intelligence that combines development and runtime software tools to analyse, model, and monitor business processes.
Task mining combines process mining techniques and specific algorithms for case segmentation and data pattern recognition. NLP may be used to identify and extract key data, and computer vision and screen capturing may be utilised in robotic process automation (RPA) use cases to create or improve user interface logs.

Gartner identifies four AI trends that are reshaping warehouse work
Gartner has identified four types of artificial intelligence it expects to reshape warehouse operations, ranging from established forecasting tools to robots that can perform physical tasks.
The research firm said warehouses have reached an inflection point for AI adoption. It pointed to persistent labor shortages, less risky ways to pay for automation, and the growing readiness of AI and autonomous technology for daily use.
Gartner’s framework weighs how independently a system can act and how sophisticated its intelligence is. The four categories cover software that predicts demand, generative AI that creates instructions, agents that help manage workflows, and robots that handle goods.
“These four AI trends are interconnected and reflect the evolution of a more intelligent, adaptive and resilient warehouse environment,” said Federica Stufano, senior principal analyst in Gartner’s Supply Chain practice. “As labor pressures persist and AI technologies mature, organizations are moving beyond experimentation toward operational deployment.”

"Many leading intranet vendors are focused only on desk-based employees, but Staffbase's platform is built to be the frontline superapp, designed for the people who are hardest to reach. We're proud to once again be recognized as a Leader, particularly as we continue to invest deeply in bringing AI to the entire workforce. That focus is why Staffbase is the front door to work for every employee, not just those at a desk."
Backed by 11 years of enterprise deployment experience, Staffbase grounds every AI-generated response in governed, verified knowledge. Whether an employee asks a question on the factory floor or at an office desk, the response is accurate, contextual, and immediately actionable without requiring training. As a result, business priorities are turned into employee action across roles and locations, so every employee, not just those at a desk, gets the same experience.

NEW YORK & SINGAPORE, September 28, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Darwinbox today announced that it ranks among the top two HCM vendors globally for Applied AI in the 2026 Gartner® Critical Capabilities for HCM Suites for 1,000+ Employee Enterprises. The recognition follows the launch of Darwinbox Cortex, the AI-Native HCM platform, fundamentally reimagined with AI at its foundation rather than layered on top. Rebuilt from the ground up, Cortex defines a new category of HCM: moving beyond recording work to understanding, anticipating, and acting. Cortex launched with global design partners including Visteon Corporation, a Fortune 1000 enterprise, and Transcarent, and technology partners including Microsoft, Slack, and Glean.
"Darwinbox being one of only two vendors to score 3.4 or higher for Applied AI is meaningful validation of the direction we have taken with Cortex," said Chaitanya Peddi, Co-founder and Co-CEO, Darwinbox. "The next phase of AI in HR will not be defined by access to models alone. It will be defined by how deeply AI understands each organization: its people, roles, skills, policies, workflows, and permissions, and how reliably it can turn that understanding into action. Darwinbox's HCM Context Graph gives Cortex that foundation, enabling agents to reason and work across the employee lifecycle with the right governance and accountability. We believe the future of HCM is not merely a system that records how an organization works, but one that understands it and helps move work forward."
Gartner recognized Darwinbox's overall AI capabilities and strategy as a strength, highlighting the breadth of AI innovation across the platform, including more than 60 pre-built agentic and generative AI use cases, Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent2Agent (A2A) interoperability, and a no-code Agent Builder.
Cortex is the world's first HCM built on a Context Graph, a live, unified map of the organization: its people, roles, policies, workflows, and decisions. The Context Graph is what allows agents to reason across the full organizational context and act on it. For organizations, that means:
Everyone in HR becomes a builder.
HR teams describe what they need in plain language, and Cortex builds it, whether that is a process, a workflow or an agent. The Context Graph unifies organizational context, system capabilities and HR expertise, so AI reasons over live context rather than a static configuration.
Trusted autonomy, within set limits.
Agents reason and execute within an organization's existing permissions and governance. Every action is transparent, policy-aware, and accountable, leaving behind a receipt of every decision. That is how Cortex unlocks trusted autonomy that compounds, within the limits the organization sets.
Risks and opportunities surfaced early.
Cortex fundamentally changes how HR sees what is happening by continuously sensing patterns across roles, modules, and moments of the employee lifecycle that might otherwise remain hidden. It surfaces emerging risks and opportunities early, giving HR the ability to anticipate and act while outcomes can still be shaped.
Across organizations, Darwinbox AI is already changing how HR operates: understanding context, surfacing what matters earlier, and enabling HR to act at scale. At a full-service bank serving more than 18 million customers, time to hire fell from 33 days to 17 days, a 48% reduction, while HR queries dropped 31% year over year, with more than 43,000 interactions through Darwinbox AI.

Gartner Stock Rises 41% in Three Months: Here's What You Should Know
Gartner, Inc. IT stock has rallied 41% over the past three months, significantly outperforming the industry's 16.8% growth and the Zacks S&P 500 Composite's 5.2% return.
Let us delve deeper into the factors that have contributed to the company's outperformance.
Gartner is benefiting from rising demand for AI-related guidance across chief information officers, human resources, sales, marketing and other enterprise functions. Insights revenues increased 2.1% year over year, or 1% on a foreign-currency-neutral basis, to $1.29 billion, while contribution rose 4% to $999 million. The contribution margin expanded 150 basis points to 77.5%, highlighting the scalability of its subscription-based research model.
Conference revenues grew 15.5%, or 14.2% on a foreign-currency-neutral basis, to $244 million, with contributions up 19.6% to $145 million and margin expanding 210 basis points to 59.5%. As enterprises shift spending toward AI strategy, cybersecurity, implementation and return on investment, Gartner should benefit from deeper client engagement and higher demand for its research and advisory services. This backdrop remains supportive of revenue growth and further operating leverage.
Contract Value Growth & Retention Support Expansion
IT's total contract value (CV) grew 2% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, accelerating 70 basis points sequentially, while ex-U.S. federal CV increased 3.3%. Global CV reached $5.28 billion, up 1.7% year over year and 0.3% sequentially on a foreign-currency-neutral basis, pointing to gradually stabilizing subscription demand. Global Business Sales CV rose 3.3% year over year and 1.2% sequentially to $1.28 billion. Global wallet retention improved to 98.2% from 97.7% in the prior quarter, while client retention increased to 85.2% from 85% sequentially and 84.6% a year earlier. Contract value per enterprise advanced to $414,000 from $376,000. Improving retention and higher spend per client should create more opportunities for account expansion, license growth and new business, supporting further contract value acceleration over time.
Profitability & Cash Flow Support Financial Flexibility
Gartner's adjusted EBITDA, excluding the divested operation, increased 6.4% year over year or 4.4% on a foreign-currency-neutral basis, to $466 million in the second quarter of 2026. GAAP operating income rose 15.7% to $378.5 million, with the operating margin improving to 22.6% from 19.4%, aided by lower service, product development and administrative expenses. Net income increased 14.4% to $275.5 million, while EPS climbed 33.1% to $4.14, supported by a lower share count. Operating cash flow grew 3.8% to $398 million and free cash flow advanced 8.9% to $378 million. Margin expansion, earnings growth and healthy cash generation collectively strengthen Gartner's financial flexibility and support continued shareholder returns.

Gartner expected to beat contract value estimates as UBS sees room for guidance upgrade
Gartner expected to beat contract value estimates as UBS sees room for guidance upgrade Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock
Gartner Inc (NYSE:IT), the research and advisory company, is expected to report third-quarter contract value growth of 2.5%, slightly above the 2.3% Visible Alpha estimate, according to UBS.
The analyst expects net new contract value to increase by $58 million in the quarter, down slightly from its previous estimate of $60 million.
Contract value growth excluding federal business is forecast to slow by about 40 basis points to 3.1% from 3.5% in the second quarter, reflecting a difficult renewal backdrop and selling environment.
UBS expects net new contract value excluding federal business of $45 million, down from its previous estimate of $60 million and last year's $62 million.
Federal net new contract value is forecast at $13 million, compared with $11 million in the second quarter and a $49 million decline a year earlier, helped by seasonally higher government procurement in the third quarter.
UBS expects Gartner to raise its 2026 revenue guidance to at least $6.380 billion from $6.375 billion, although that would remain below the $6.395 billion analyst estimate.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance is expected to increase to at least $1.605 billion from $1.570 billion, while adjusted earnings per share guidance could rise to $14.55+ from $14.00+.
UBS expects the guidance increase to be driven primarily by margin contingency, while a $5 million increase in each of Conferences and Consulting would more than offset a $5 million foreign exchange headwind to Insights revenue.
The analyst models just under $200 million of share buybacks in the third quarter, noticeably below the levels of recent quarters, amid a potential moderation in repurchase activity.
UBS trimmed its 2026 adjusted earnings per share estimate to $15.04 from $15.14, citing slightly lower fourth-quarter revenue from Conferences and foreign exchange.
For 2027, UBS cut its adjusted earnings per share estimate to $16.01 from $16.05 because of lower revenue, partly offset by a slightly higher margin and lower share count.
UBS said indicators were mixed, with Gartner job openings about 10% below their mid-July peak, while the Business Roundtable CEO Index rose to 94.4 from 90.7 in the second quarter, its highest level since early 2022.

our ability to pay our debt obligations; the impact of global economic and geopolitical conditions, including inflation (and related monetary policy by governments in response to inflation) and recession; uncertain effects, both direct and indirect, of changes and volatility in tariffs and trade policies; risks associated with the creditworthiness, budget cuts, priorities and shutdown of governments and agencies; additional risks associated with international operations, including foreign currency fluctuations; the impact on our business resulting from changes in international conditions, including those resulting from tensions in the Middle East, the war in Ukraine and current and future sanctions imposed by governments or other authorities; the impact of restructuring and other charges on our businesses and operations; our ability to meet sustainability commitments and comply with applicable regulatory requirements, as well as potential reactions by customers to these commitments; the impact of changes in tax policy (including global minimum tax legislation) and heightened scrutiny from various taxing authorities globally; changes to laws and regulations; and other risks and uncertainties described under “Risk Factors” in our most recent Annual Report on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q and Current Reports on Form 8-K, which can be found on Gartner’s website at https://investor.gartner.com and the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov. Forward-looking statements included herein speak only as of the date hereof and Gartner disclaims any obligation to revise or update such statements to reflect events or circumstances after the date hereof or to reflect the occurrence of unanticipated events or circumstances, except as required by applicable law.
Certain financial measures used in this Press Release are not defined by U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”) and as such are considered non-GAAP financial measures. We provide these measures to enhance the user’s overall understanding of the Company’s current financial performance and the Company’s prospects for the future. Investors are cautioned that these non-GAAP financial measures may not be defined in the same manner by other companies and, as a result, may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures used by other companies. Also, these non-GAAP financial measures should not be construed as alternatives, or superior, to other measures determined in accordance with GAAP. The non-GAAP financial measures used in this Press Release are defined below.
Adjusted Revenues: Represents GAAP revenues less revenues from our Digital Markets divested operation. We believe Adjusted Revenues is an important measure of our recurring operations as it provides a more accurate period-over period comparison of trends in revenues.
Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin: Represents GAAP net income (loss) adjusted for: (i) interest expense, net; (ii) tax provision (benefit); (iii) gain on event cancellation insurance claims, as applicable; (iv) other (income) expense, net; (v) stock-based compensation expense; (vi) depreciation, amortization, and accretion; (vii) goodwill impairment and other asset impairments, as applicable, (viii) workforce reduction expenses and certain other non-recurring items and (ix) gain/loss on divestitures, as applicable. Adjusted EBITDA Margin represents Adjusted EBITDA divided by GAAP Revenue. We believe Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin are important measures of our recurring operations as they exclude items not representative of our core operating results.
Adjusted EBITDA Excluding Divested Operation and Adjusted EBITDA Margin Excluding Divested Operation: Represents Adjusted EBITDA as defined above less EBITDA from our Digital Markets divested operation. Adjusted EBITDA Margin Excluding Divested Operation represents Adjusted EBITDA Excluding Divested Operation divided by Adjusted Revenue. We believe Adjusted EBITDA Excluding Divested Operation and Adjusted EBITDA Margin Excluding Divested Operation are important measures of our recurring operations as it provides a more accurate and consistent period-over period comparison of our results.
Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS: Represents GAAP net income (loss) and diluted net income (loss) per share adjusted for the impact of certain items directly related to acquisitions and other non-recurring items. These adjustments include (on a per share basis, in the case of Adjusted EPS): (i) the amortization of acquired intangibles*; (ii) workforce reduction expenses and other non-recurring items; (iii) gain on event cancellation insurance claims, as applicable; (iv) the non-cash (gain) loss on de-designated interest rate swaps, as applicable; (v) goodwill impairment and other asset impairments, as applicable, (vi) gain/loss on divestitures, as applicable. and (vii) the related tax impact. We believe Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS are important measures of our recurring operations as they exclude items that may not be indicative of our core operating results.
* The Company excludes amortization of acquired intangibles because it is generally a fixed non-cash expense that can be significantly impacted by the timing and/or size of acquisitions and management does not use it to evaluate core operating results. Although the Company excludes the amortization of acquired intangibles from Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS, management believes that it is important for investors to understand that such intangible assets were recorded as part of acquisition accounting and contribute to revenue generation.
Free Cash Flow: Represents cash provided by operating activities determined in accordance with GAAP less payments for capital expenditures. We believe Free Cash Flow is an important measure of the recurring cash generated by the Company’s core operations that may be available to be used to repay debt obligations, repurchase our stock, invest in future growth through new business development activities, or make acquisitions.
Foreign Currency Neutral (FX Neutral): We provide foreign currency neutral dollar amounts and percentages for our contract values, revenues, certain expenses, and other metrics. These foreign currency neutral dollar amounts and percentages eliminate the effects of exchange rate fluctuations and thus provide a more accurate and meaningful trend in the underlying data being measured. We calculate foreign currency neutral dollar amounts by converting the underlying amounts in local currency for different periods into U.S. dollars by applying the same foreign exchange rates to all periods presented.

Can CDW Corporation Restore Margin Momentum in the Second Half?
CDW Corporation CDW has entered the second half of 2026 with a focus on improving operating leverage and expense efficiency after delivering solid second-quarter results. The company reported second-quarter net sales of $6.6 billion, up 10% year over year, while gross profit increased 6% to $1.3 billion. Non-GAAP operating income rose 7% to $556 million, and non-GAAP earnings per share increased 12% to $2.91. However, gross margin declined 70 basis points (bps) year over year to 20.1%, reflecting a greater contribution from large hardware infrastructure opportunities related to modernization and AI readiness, particularly among enterprise customers, along with a lower relative contribution from services.
On the last earnings call, management highlighted that the gross-margin pressure was primarily a function of business mix rather than like-for-like pricing pressure. CDW maintained pricing discipline and continued to pass through price increases, while the growing mix of infrastructure products, larger-dollar orders and enterprise customers carried relatively lower margins. At the same time, netted-down revenue streams increased 16.1% and accounted for 35.9% of gross profit, up 300 bps year over year. Services grew only 1% as customers prioritized hardware and cloud investments and deployment timing affected demand, although CDW expects life-cycle and professional services activity to increase as customers move from procurement toward implementation and management.
The second half is expected to bring greater benefits from CDW's Geared for Growth initiatives. Second-quarter non-GAAP SG&A represented 57.9% of gross profit, down 20 bps year over year and 410 bps sequentially. Management said the second-quarter improvement in operating leverage largely reflected expense discipline and broader efficiency measures, while the more significant benefits from Geared for Growth are expected to emerge in the back half. The company expects both operating leverage and its expense ratio to improve sequentially through the second half and into 2027.
For 2026, CDW expects gross profit to grow in the mid-single digits, although second-half gross margins are projected to remain below year-ago levels because of product and end-market mix. Third-quarter non-GAAP SG&A is expected to decline sequentially, helping reduce operating expenses as a percentage of gross profit both year over year and sequentially. Management also expects services demand to strengthen as current infrastructure projects progress into implementation, supporting its expectation for improving operating leverage during the second half.
ServiceNow, Inc.'s NOW margins remain under pressure as rising AI adoption and greater reliance on hyperscaler infrastructure increase costs. In the second quarter of 2026, non-GAAP total gross margin declined to 78% from 81% a year earlier, while subscription gross margin fell 250 bps to 80.5%. Despite the pressure, non-GAAP operating margin remained stable at 29.5%, supported by revenue outperformance and disciplined spending. For 2026, ServiceNow continues to target an 81% non-GAAP subscription gross margin and 31.5% operating margin. Management expects AI-driven efficiencies, including roughly $500 million in internal savings, to help offset infrastructure and integration-related margin pressures.
Accenture plc's ACN margins remained relatively stable in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, despite ongoing investments in AI, talent and acquisitions. Gross margin was 32.8%, slightly below 32.9% in the year-ago quarter, reflecting continued cost pressures from its labor-intensive delivery model and evolving AI-led services. However, operating income increased 6% year over year to $3.18 billion, while operating margin expanded 20 bps to 17% from 16.8%. SG&A expenses declined to 15.8% of revenues from 16%. Strong Managed Services growth and disciplined cost management supported profitability, although AI-driven delivery changes and higher acquisition spending could influence margins going forward.
Avnet, Inc.'s AVT margin profile is improving as higher volumes, favorable mix and operating leverage support profitability. Adjusted operating margin expanded to 3.8% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, up 73 bps sequentially and 129 bps year over year. Electronic Components margin reached 4.1%, while Farnell's margin rose to 9% from 4.3% a year earlier, supported by a higher mix of on-board components. Management expects Farnell to reach double-digit margins before the end of fiscal 2027 and consolidated SG&A as a percentage of gross profit to fall below 60%. However, gross margin remains sensitive to regional mix and pricing dynamics.

IT leaders are the midst of an identity crisis. Long seen as back-office superheroes, some IT leaders now find themselves expected to serve as innovators, evangelists and even the “fun people.”
“I didn’t know that we were the fun people, man. Like, I was supposed to do one thing, now I have to worry about if it’s fun or not?” said Carollo Engineers CIO Andrew Ivey to his fellow panelist, St. Luke’s University Health Network Associate CISO Krista Arndt.
The two were having an introspective but casual discussion about how they were responding to all of the changes in the workplace and IT — especially those wrought by artificial intelligence.
But the setup for this conference conversation was different. The panel, which took place onstage during the 2026 CDW Summit in Dallas, had a podcast aesthetic to it and it was dubbed “CDW OTR (On the Record).” The two had big podcast mics in front of them, and Arndt was dressed more casually and sitting cross-legged on the couch. This could have been a conversation livestreaming from YouTube or Twitch.

The idea that IT leaders would present themselves in such a down-to-earth manner would have seemed out of place more than five years ago. But this change in tone and style is a sign of the times. And the idea that it’s important to infuse fun, excitement or positivity into their IT management styles was one that Arndt clearly embraced more easily than Ivey, who viewed his role as an IT leader as more of an honest broker and a skeptic — especially when it comes to the AI hype cycle.
“I think it’s your responsibility to be the voice of reason and to help guide this. And if you don’t have a skeptic in the room, then guess what your job is: to be the skeptic,” said Ivey. “If you have a skeptic in the room, then it’s probably not helpful for you also to be a skeptic. But you need one. And so, go find one, bring them in the room, just so they can poke holes in this thing early on. And I think you’ll survive and build a bulletproof project if you just bring in a naysayer early.”
Arndt said she prioritizes a highly collaborative but honest and authentic approach to IT leadership. For her, having a positive relationship and effective communication with her non-IT counterparts is critical to her role as a security leader.
“Our technology organization has a phenomenal relationship with our hospital leadership, and they talk constantly,” said Arndt. “It’s something that we focus on a lot in security: speaking the language of people that we serve so they really understand what’s going on.”
Those conversations, which might seem more casual than they were in the past, are extremely valuable in Arndt’s pursuit of getting her non-IT counterparts to receive her concerns about risk management.
“Having those open conversations where you can just be yourself and feel like you’re not just trying to put on a show for your leadership … I do see that happening,” added Arndt. “They know there’s a lot of unknowns, but they’re really excited to investigate those reasonably and from a risk-balance basis.”

Linking AI With Strategic Business Imperatives
As she walked out to the main stage to welcome the more than 600 attendees at the Sheraton Dallas Hotel, CDW Chief Commercial Officer Liz Connelly acknowledged that everyone in tech has been talking a lot about AI, and that many people are eager for the next step.
“OK, we know you’ve heard a lot about AI,” said Connelly. “We won’t be spending time simply admiring the opportunities and challenges around AI. We’ll be sharing our well-informed point of view on what to prioritize, what to build and what to do next. Because the question is no longer whether AI will change business. The question is how organizations can use AI to deliver real and measurable business ambition outcomes.”
To highlight just how CDW was putting its money where its mouth is, Connelly brought out the company’s recently hired chief strategy and transformation officer, Hang Tan.
Tan, who has been tasked with advancing CDW’s AI strategy, highlighted how CDW has decided to treat itself as “Customer Zero” as it deploys and learns from its own AI implementations.
CDW Chief Strategy and Transformation Officer Hang Tan speaks about CDW’s six AI imperatives, which are informed by its “Customer Zero” approach to AI, at the 2026 CDW Summit.
During his presentation, Tan shared six core AI imperatives that CDW has developed that he believes can also help guide its customers’ thinking around AI:
AI-ready infrastructure: “This is more than just securing GPU capacity, because when we're when we're talking about agents, agents will put entirely new demands across all of your infrastructure — your public cloud, your data center, your network, and your endpoints.”
Getting your data ready for AI: “This is all about giving AI secure access to your unique business context. But then, once you do that, your AI will start to generate data. How do you manage the AI-generated data, and how do you extract insights from that data?”
Activating AI in existing software platforms: “As these platforms introduce new agentic capabilities, you have a very tricky or important set of decisions to make: Where does it make sense to activate AI within each of your platforms, but where does it make sense to actually develop AI capabilities on top and across your platforms?”
Adopting assistants and agentic platforms. “Everybody here in the room are well down the path of adopting AI assistants, but the magic really happens when you move past the, ‘Hey, let's give everybody Copilot and have them experiment on their own,’ to how do you get to shared learning, shared experimentation, shared skills, shared agents? That’s where the benefit, the productivity, will really scale.”
Security: “How do you evolve your identity and your security controls to extend beyond just users, devices, but to also extend to agents?”
Financial discipline around AI: “It’s more than just tracking what the spend is or controlling the spend because, remember, if you really want to demonstrate business outcomes, you need to instrument both the AI, but also instrument your processes.”
The tone that CDW’s leadership was taking with AI was clear and focused on outcomes, and a sign that IT is intent on getting to a place of real progress when it comes to AI. The tech industry has spent a lot of time talking about how AI will change things, but many in IT are eager to see more proof of this change — and not just doomsday warnings or the frothy hype.
Humanoid Robotics Is Funny Stuff, but Also Serious Business
As Arndt and Ivey debated the state of IT and how drastically AI will reshape their industry, CDW Senior Vice President of Vertical Markets Mike Grisamore interrupted their conversation to bring out a special guest: CDW’s own humanoid robot, named CH3T.
The robot actually made its debut six months earlier, at the 2026 HIMSS Global Health Conference & Exhibition in Las Vegas. Nonetheless, the robot was an instant favorite with the audience at the Summit as it teetered out onto the stage wearing scrub pants and a Team USA hat, a nod to CDW’s role as an official sponsor of the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.
CH3T comes out on stage to hang out with CDW’s panelists and moderators during the CDW OTR mainstage event at the 2026 CDW Summit.
“CH3T, by the way, those are some sweet scrubs you got,” teased Grisamore. “Apparently, when CH3T first joined us, CH3T came out, and having CH3T without pants on was a little disturbing to some of the nurses. So, CH3T now has scrubs, which are pretty sweet. And I know normally you wear your Crocs, like every good clinician does, but I do like the CDW red.”
While the bit between CH3T and the hosts was fun, and audience members seemed to marvel at the technical prowess of a robot that walked and responded to human interaction in real time, Grisamore noted that despite the lighthearted banter between him and the humanoid robot, CH3T was more than entertainment. He represented a meaningful investment on the part of CDW in promise of physical AI.
“We think about physical AI, and looking at them just as platforms, because we know that investing kind of in what’s next, it doesn’t always fit into everyone’s immediate budget,” said Grisamore. “Not that we have a massive budget to do it, but the opportunity to carve out a little bit and start thinking about, ‘All right, how do we take CH3T, or, you know, two generations past CH3T, and start thinking about, ‘All right, what are the use cases where there is a return on investment?’”
“We’ve got one of CH3T’s brothers that is pushing wheelchairs around, and we’re thinking about transport. We’re thinking about utilization, because CH3T, when he’s not pushing someone around in a wheelchair, he could be going and restocking supply closets,” added Grisamore.
Maybe CH3T is proof that IT can be about a little bit of fun and a little bit of business at the same time. And that IT is in a place where it can do more, be more and achieve more than it ever has in the past.

CDW Corporation CDW has stepped up capital returns in 2026, with share repurchases gaining notable momentum even as free cash flow (FCF) conversion remained below its historical framework during the first half. In the second quarter, the company returned $344 million to shareholders through buybacks and another $80 million through dividends.
First-half repurchases totaled approximately $545 million, already approaching the $653 million deployed during all of 2025 and exceeding the $500 million repurchased in each of 2023 and 2024. The company also added $1 billion to its share repurchase authorization during the quarter, leaving more than $1.1 billion of remaining capacity and providing considerable flexibility for further buybacks.
The sustainability of this faster capital-return pace will partly depend on a recovery in cash generation. Adjusted free cash flow was $278 million in the first half, representing 42% of non-GAAP net income and falling below management's long-term rule of thumb of converting 80-90% of non-GAAP net income into cash.
On the last earnings call, management attributed the shortfall primarily to working-capital timing as CDW invested to support hardware-driven growth and customer demand amid elevated pricing. Inventory increased by roughly $400 million from year-end, but management expects to rationalize inventory as supply conditions become more normalized, making inventory reduction the biggest variable behind an anticipated improvement in second-half free cash flow.
CDW's balance sheet also provides some support for continued shareholder distributions. Net leverage ended the quarter at 2.5X, comfortably within management's 2X-3X target range, while liquidity was $2 billion. The company continues to target a dividend payout of roughly 25% of non-GAAP net income and remains active in evaluating acquisitions that broaden its capabilities and customer relevance.
Meanwhile, Geared for Growth initiatives are expected to improve expense efficiency and operating leverage during the second half and into 2027, potentially strengthening future investment and capital-deployment capacity.
ServiceNow NOW generated $2.257 billion of operating cash flow in the first half of 2026 and continues to target a 35% FCF margin for 2026.
